itemListElement.name: How to Get Your AI Startup Into TechCrunch in 2026

mainEntity.name: How do you get an AI startup covered by TechCrunch in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pitch one reporter whose beat matches your story, offer a genuine exclusive on a verifiable milestone, keep the pitch under 150 words, and give them 48 hours before going elsewhere. Before pitching, read the last five pieces that specific reporter has published to understand what angle they are currently building. TechCrunch responds to story ingredients: a surprising funding round, a category-defining product, proprietary data, or a founder argument that reframes a trend. The pitch is a short, human note, not a forwarded press release.

mainEntity.name: Should I offer TechCrunch an exclusive or use an embargo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Offer an exclusive when the story is strong enough to carry the publication on its own and you can hold the news for 48 hours. Use an embargo when you need coordinated coverage across multiple outlets simultaneously, typically for a product launch rather than a funding announcement. Exclusives give reporters a reason to prioritise your story; embargoes spread coverage across the same day. If your exclusive is passed on or unanswered after 48 hours, move to an embargo across two or three targets without following up aggressively.

mainEntity.name: What kinds of AI startup stories does TechCrunch actually publish?

acceptedAnswer.text: In 2026, TechCrunch prioritises funding announcements with a clear market narrative, category-defining product launches, data-led enterprise stories with proprietary numbers, and analytical founder op-eds under the member editorial track. AI wrapper products built on top of public foundation models with no proprietary data, and AI copilot pitches in already-crowded categories, rarely land without an unusual angle. The story needs to be about what the milestone means for the market, not just what happened inside the company.

mainEntity.name: How long should a TechCrunch pitch be?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under 150 words for the body. Three short paragraphs: the story in two sentences, the connection to what that reporter has been covering, and the offer with the ask. Anything longer signals you do not know your story well enough to condense it. The press release, the fact sheet, and any supporting metrics are attachments or linked documents, not the pitch itself.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if TechCrunch passes on my story?

acceptedAnswer.text: First, distinguish between an explicit pass and no response. No response after 48 hours allows one brief follow-up. If they pass explicitly, extract the reason and act on it: not enough traction means return with numbers in three months; already covered the angle means reframe or wait. Then move to the next outlet on your list, which might be Forbes Technology, Bloomberg, Wired, or on the crypto side, CoinDesk. The mechanics of getting featured in CoinDesk follow the same reporter-first, exclusive-first logic.
